notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, as the county reported them in its Annual Financial Report to the Iowa Department of Management. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included.
Spending is reported by service area. Capital projects have no service area, so they are spread over the county's other spending in proportion.

Borrowing, transfers between funds, refunded debt and sales of capital assets are left out. Debt service also leaves out $1,359,657 paid with new borrowing the county did not spend on capital that year, most likely refinancing or a rolled-over note.
Administration and government services to residents (recorder, treasurer, elections) count as overhead.
Debt outstanding is not in the Department of Management's published data, so no debt figure is given and debt is not scored.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Iowa county candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Iowa yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
